**6B.9 Research Note: Olaf Scholz in 2024**

**Bottom line**
Mostly yes, but not robustly. Scholz did build and operate through some real institutional reforms in 2024, especially whole-of-government risk planning, administrative traceability, digital service modernization, and formal review mechanisms. The main limitation is durability: coalition collapse and year-end parliamentary loss of confidence badly weakened continuity, so several gains look real but fragile rather than fully insulated from his personal rule.

**Accepted claims**
- **National Security Strategy** | Federal Government | 14 Jun 2023, operative in 2024 | [URL](https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-en/aktuelles/national-security-strategy-2196356) | Scholz’s first National Security Strategy is explicitly a “systematic overall approach” that includes diplomacy, police, fire brigades, civil protection, cyber security, supply-chain resilience, and pandemic prevention. That is the clearest structural evidence of institution-building rather than personalized rule. | `6B.9` `6B.6` `6B.5`

- **Bundeskabinett results on executive footprint** | Bundesregierung | 6 Mar 2024 | [URL](https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-de/aktuelles/bundeskabinett-ergebnisse-2263572) | The cabinet adopted traceability reforms to implement the “executive footprint” and “synopsis,” improving how draft laws and outside influence can be traced. That is a concrete anti-capture, pro-accountability institutional reform. | `6B.9` `6B.5` `6B.4`

- **Online access law reform** | Deutscher Bundestag | 23 Feb 2024 | [URL](https://www.bundestag.de/dokumente/textarchiv/2024/kw08-de-onlinezugangsgesetz-990686) | The revised OZG strengthened federal-Länder structures and modern, user-friendly digital service delivery through the portal network and shared base services. This is durable service-infrastructure work, not just short-term spending. | `6B.9` `6B.5` `6B.2`

- **Bundeswehr missions evaluation** | Federal Foreign Office / Federal Ministry of Defence | 26 Jun 2024 | [URL](https://www.auswaertiges-amt.de/en/newsroom/news/2664958-2664958) | The government’s first overarching evaluation of Bundeswehr missions abroad used uniform criteria and identified improvement needs, including better civilian-military coordination and more realistic goals. That is direct evidence of institutional review and correction. | `6B.9` `6B.5` `6B.6`

- **Stable financial policy / growth initiative** | Federal Government | 24 Apr 2024 | [URL](https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-de/aktuelles/stable-financial-policy-2273918) | Scholz said fiscal policy was moving from crisis management back to debt-brake compliance while still maintaining high investment and raising growth potential. This suggests an attempt to normalize rule-based state capacity rather than operate only through ad hoc crisis improvisation. | `6B.9` `6B.4` `6B.5`

- **Budget 2025 growth package** | Federal Government | 5 Jul 2024 | [URL](https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-en/service/archive/budget-2025-2298116) | Scholz presented a jointly negotiated 49-measure package built around modernization, infrastructure, tax relief, social housing, renewables, and growth. The existence of a concrete implementation package is evidence of institutionalized policy design, though not proof of durable success. | `6B.9` `6B.2` `6B.4` `6B.5`

- **Chancellor summer press conference** | Federal Government | 24 Jul 2024 | [URL](https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-en/service/archive/chancellor-summer-press-conference-2024-2301040) | Scholz said the growth initiative contained 49 individual measures and then took extensive public questions. That is modest but real accountability behavior tied to a rule-based reform program. | `6B.9` `6B.5` `6B.7`

- **Free press / scrutiny support** | Bundesregierung | 3 Jun 2024 | [URL](https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-de/service/newsletter-und-abos/bulletin/scholz-journalistenschule-2290636) | Scholz praised investigative reporting, critical distance, and press freedom as essential to democracy. This supports a broader institutional environment for scrutiny that can outlast a single leader. | `6B.9` `6B.5` `6B.7`

**Counterweights**
- **Coalition collapse** | Reuters via Investing.com | 6 Nov 2024 | [URL](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/explainergerman-coalition-collapses-what-comes-next-3706936) | The coalition collapse triggered political chaos and weakened policy continuity late in 2024. This is the main practical counterweight: even good institutional designs became harder to sustain. | `6B.9`

- **No-confidence vote** | Deutscher Bundestag | 16 Dec 2024 | [URL](https://www.bundestag.de/dokumente/textarchiv/2024/kw47-vertrauensfrage-1030198) | Parliament’s loss of confidence confirmed year-end instability and reduced policy continuity. That undercuts the claim that Scholz had already built institutions durable enough to carry far beyond his own term. | `6B.9` `6B.4`

- **BND surveillance ruling** | Bundesverfassungsgericht | 8 Nov 2024 | [URL](https://www.bundesverfassungsgericht.de/SharedDocs/Pressemitteilungen/EN/2024/bvg24-093.html) | The Court found parts of the BND framework unconstitutional and oversight inadequate. This is a structural weakness in state institutions and a real negative for durability and clean oversight. | `6B.9` `6B.5` `6B.8`

- **Confidential 5G process** | Reuters via onvista | 23 May 2024 | [URL](https://www.onvista.de/news/2024/05-23-bericht-regierung-vertagt-entscheidung-ueber-strengere-vorschriften-im-5g-netz-0-20-26275293) | Reuters reported the 5G security decision was handled confidentially and ministries declined public comment. That is precautionary, but it weakens the transparency of the institutional process. | `6B.9` `6B.5`

**Search gap**
I found strong evidence of institution-building in process and design, but much less direct evidence of durability beyond Scholz personally. The clearest missing piece is post-tenure survivability evidence: whether these reforms continued to function after the 2024 coalition break. The record is enough for a partial yes, not for a high-confidence durable-institutions verdict.
